title: Factorising
opener_concept: Splitting 8 red and 12 white roses into as many identical bouquets as possible (HCF 4 -> 4 bouquets of 2 and 3) names taking out a common factor: 8x + 12 = 4(2x + 3).
notes: Fresh-solved all 20 multiple_choice problems (8 bronze / 7 silver / 5 gold) by expanding every option with sympy: every stored correct answer (option 0) matches its display; no wrong solutions, no degenerate or messy-decimal problems, no within-tier duplicates. So problems_fixed is empty. Full guided conversion added: tier_guides (bronze common-factor, silver x^2+bx+c, gold difference-of-two-squares/beyond, fresh examples 12x+8, x^2+9x+20, x^2-36), guided.opener (bouquet HCF hook), guided.teach walks (bronze 9x+12, silver x^2+8x+15, gold 4x^2-25, all fresh, not in bank), per-problem hint, and guided_steps on every problem with a phase:'substitute' completion boundary. Repairs beyond the bank maths (counted in issues_resolved): (1) cleaned method_card which contained an em dash ('common factor first - always') that would have failed the style gate, trimmed to the slim reference shape; (2) replaced every problem's broken misconceptions (old ones had no 'expect' key and were solution-reveals) with honest per-distractor diagnostics whose expect is the exact wrong option index, each error committed and verified. Not-fully-factorised distractors (e.g. 2(2a+6), (2x+6)(x+2), 5x(x^2-4)) are framed as incomplete_factorisation, not wrong-value. No figures added: Factorising is a purely textual algebra topic and a GCSE paper prints no figure for it; opener uses pure-imagination phrasing so nothing is claimed that is not shown. Preserved byte-for-byte: related_videos ([]), worked_examples (3), topic_links ({prerequisites:[]}).
